title: Pardoned felon Josh Smith tapped to lead Tennessee’s correction department | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A pardoned felon who served as second in command of the federal Bureau of Prisons is next in line to lead the embattled Tennessee Department of Correction, which has come under scrutiny most recently for thefailed execution of Christa Pike.

Tennessee Gov.-elect Marsha Blackburn named Josh Smith as the next TDOC commissioner in a string of appointments announced this week.

A businessman and prison reform advocate, Smithserved five years in federal prison for drug trafficking-related charges in the late 1990s and had several other felony convictions in his youth,according to his website.He’s credited Christianity and the guidance of highly educated white-collar criminals for his eventual success after leaving federal prison.

Smith takes over a department rocked by Pike’s unprecedented experience surviving lethal injection, which led to apause on executions in Tennesseeand a national debate over the humanity and reliability of capital punishment methods.

“Josh brings a distinctive combination of executive leadership, firsthand correctional experience, and an understanding of the challenges facing our prison system,”Blackburn said announcing Smith’s appointment on X.

President DonaldTrump pardoned Smith in 2021for his 1998 federal conviction, and he later took a role as deputy director of the Federal Bureau of Prisons in 2025. Smith thanked Trump for being “willing to take a chance that no President before him had taken.”

Smith has publicly acknowledged his status as a convicted felon might’ve rubbed some BOP employees the wrong way.

“When I entered the BOP, I knew my appointment would be a shock to the system. There were people from the beginning who did not believe someone like me belonged in this position,” Smith said in a statement announcing his departure in August.

Smith visited over 70 federal facilities during his time as BOP’s second in command, according to a recent statement. He stepped down after about a year in the position, though it’s unclear why.

The prison reform advocate has also previously worked with Tennessee correction officials. Gov. Bill Lee appointed him to the steering committee of a criminal justice task force in 2019, serving with TDOC leadership and state officials to develop legislative and budgetary recommendations for public safety and reentry issues.

TDOC spokesperson Dorinda Carter told CNN, “We look forward to working with Josh and offering him our full support.”

An interim commissioner currently sits in the top correction position in Tennessee after the last commissioner,Frank Strada, resigned in the wake of Pike’s failed execution – the second botched execution in the state this year.

Lee canceled the last execution slated for this year and called for an independent review of Pike’s failed execution.

The state Attorney General’s Office retained a former US attorney, Ed Stanton, to conduct that review, which is still ongoing. Stanton previously reviewed the state’s lethal injection protocol in 2022, also at the request of Lee.

It’s unclear how long the moratorium will hold as Blackburnhas publicly saidshe’ll reinstate the use of the electric chair when she takes office.

Attorneys for Pike are still fighting to commute her death sentence that hangs in the balance. She’s currently housed in a prison infirmary following a 10-day hospitalization recovering from the effects of the failed lethal injection, according to court filings.

Pike’s legal team did not return a request for comment on Smith’s appointment.

In a statement announcing his position Monday, Smith acknowledged challenges facing the correction department he’ll inherit come January but did not specifically mention capital punishment.

“Tennessee’s correctional system faces significant challenges, including staffing shortages, institutional safety, and the need to strengthen leadership throughout the organization. I believe we can address these challenges by empowering our employees, establishing clear expectations, developing leaders, and maintaining an unwavering commitment to public safety,”Smith said in a LinkedIn post.

CNN has reached out to Smith for further comment.
